newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-THIRD ROUND OF BUICK CHALLENGE RAINED OUT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THIRD ROUND OF BUICK CHALLENGE RAINED OUT.

text.p: The Buick Challenge golf tournament was shortened to 54 holes after torrential rain stopped play during the third round Saturday.
Barely half the field had teed off when players were forced from the Callaway Gardens course at 11.35 a.m.
Subsequent rain left the course unplayable for the rest of the day, so officials rescheduled the third round to resume early Sunday.
It is the second consecutive week and the third time in four weeks on the PGA Tour that an event has been reduced to 54 holes because of rain.
"The forecast for tomorrow is a lot better. As the day goes on we're probably going to see some sunshine," said Ben Nelson, tournament director for the PGA Tour.
Only five of 85 players completed the third round before play was halted.
Second-round leaders Len Mattiace, Davis Love, Michael Bradley, Fred Funk and John Maginnes, all on 10-under-par 134, had not teed off.
Craig Stadler and Sean Murphy made the biggest moves, gaining five strokes in 15 and 14 holes respectively to move six under.
